html:
Sarazm is an ancient settlement in the Zeravshan valley of Tajikistan, near Panjakent, lived in from about 3500 to 2000 BCE. It is one of the oldest towns in Central Asia.

Its people farmed, herded and, above all, worked metal and stone: copper, tin and turquoise from the mountains nearby. Finds of shells from the Indian Ocean, and pottery like that of Baluchistan, the Oxus civilisation and the Iranian plateau, show it was part of trade networks that stretched far beyond the valley, long before the Silk Road.

A rich grave found there, of a woman buried with ornaments, became known as the Princess of Sarazm. The site was found in 1976 and became Tajikistan's first World Heritage Site. Later the same valley was the heart of Sogdia.
sum: Sarazm is an ancient settlement in the Zeravshan valley of Tajikistan, near Panjakent, lived in from about 3500 to 2000 BCE. It is one of the oldest towns in Central Asia.
